inputArtifacts.title: Imvusa Research Report (Stage 1)
inputArtifacts.summary: Imvusa Furniture (imvusa.net) is a South African custom furniture, reupholstery, and interior services business operating from two locations (George and Bloemfontein). It is a lead-generation/consultation business (custom, quoted work) with no ecommerce functionality, which is appropriate for this business model. The site communicates its service range clearly, but our audit found two real, directly-observed data inconsistencies in contact information between the homepage and the Contact Us page (a phone number mismatch for the George office and an address mismatch for the Bloemfontein office), plus two content-quality issues: a fully duplicated services list on the Services page and inconsistent spelling of the fabric supplier's brand name ('Hertext' vs 'Hertex'). Two pages (Leather Couches, Gallery) are predominantly image-based and could not be fully assessed via text extraction alone - a visual/design review is recommended. No competitor research was conducted as part of this job; none should be assumed or fabricated.

businessContext: Imvusa Furniture is a custom furniture, repairs, reupholstery, and interior design services business based in South Africa.
Two physical locations: George and Bloemfontein.

Business model is lead-generation/consultation-based (custom, quoted work) - no shop, cart, checkout, or product-price pages exist anywhere in site navigation, which is consistent with a custom-quote services business.
Core services advertised: Furniture Repairs, Reupholstery, Custom Curtains, Headboards, Scatter Cushions, Leather Couches, Wallpaper, Ottomans.
Site names a fabric supplier partner (Hertex/Hertext Fabrics) and promotes 4 named fabric collections: ADORN, CAPPADOCIA, COASTLINES, ESQUIRE.
No pricing is published anywhere on the site - this is expected and appropriate for a custom-quote service business model, not a defect.
existingSiteFindings: Main nav consists of: Home, Leather Couches, Gallery, Services, Contact Us.
Homepage hero and service cards communicate the value proposition and full service list clearly, each with 1-2 sentence descriptions.

CONTACT MISMATCH #1 (George phone): Homepage lists George office phone as 082 468 8898; Contact Us page lists George office phone as 051 430 9883. These are different numbers for the same office - directly observed discrepancy requiring client clarification before launch.

CONTACT MISMATCH #2 (Bloemfontein address): Homepage lists Bloemfontein address as '15A Kraal Street, Old East End'; Contact Us page lists Bloemfontein address as '6 Alpha Straat, Ou Oos Einde' - a different street name and number for what should be the same office. Directly observed discrepancy requiring client clarification before launch.
Email addresses (katelyn@imvusa.net for George, theresa@imvusa.net for Bloemfontein) and Bloemfontein phone (082 824 9790) are consistent between homepage and Contact Us page.
DUPLICATE CONTENT: The Services page contains the entire 8-item services card list duplicated twice in sequence, back-to-back, with identical text both times - a content-authoring or template error.

SPELLING INCONSISTENCY: The Services page intro copy names the fabric supplier 'Hertext Fabrics' but the same page's closing CTA reads 'More Fabrics at Hertex' - two different spellings of the same partner brand within a single page.

Leather Couches page has minimal extractable text (heading + one sentence) and appears to be a predominantly image-based photo gallery; further content, layout quality, or any embedded information in image form could not be assessed via text extraction and requires a real visual/design review.
Gallery page has minimal extractable text (heading only) and appears to be a predominantly image-based portfolio; same visual-review caveat applies.

An inline image CAPTCHA challenge appears in the page text content near the contact block on both the homepage ('select the cup') and the Contact Us page ('select the heart') - these differ in prompt between pages, and the presence of CAPTCHA text within extracted page content suggests it may be rendered as accessible/plain text rather than a properly isolated challenge widget, which should be reviewed for both security and accessibility implications.
No shop, cart, checkout, or product-price pages exist anywhere in the site's navigation, consistent with a consultation/lead-generation business model.
competitorInsights: No competitor research was conducted as part of this job. No real competitor data was supplied or gathered for this analysis. Per doctrine, no competitor names, positioning claims, or market comparisons should be fabricated or assumed; this should be scoped as a separate, explicit research task if required.
risks: Contact information inconsistency (George phone number) between homepage and Contact Us page could cause prospective clients to reach a wrong or outdated number, resulting in lost leads - needs client confirmation of the correct current number before any content migration or launch.

Contact information inconsistency (Bloemfontein address) between homepage and Contact Us page could cause confusion for clients attempting to visit in person, or indicate the business has moved and one page is stale - needs client confirmation of the correct current address before any content migration or launch.
Duplicated services list on the Services page is a content-quality and possibly SEO/duplicate-content concern that should be corrected during rebuild rather than carried forward as-is.

Brand name spelling inconsistency ('Hertext' vs 'Hertex') for a named fabric supplier partner could look unprofessional to a partner brand or to visually attentive customers, and should be corrected to the accurate spelling in coordination with the client.

Leather Couches and Gallery pages being predominantly image-based means text-only audits cannot confirm accessibility (alt text), SEO metadata quality, or whether any pricing/model information is embedded in images - flagged as an open item for the visual/design review stage, not assumed to be a defect.

Presence of CAPTCHA challenge prompts as extractable plain page text (rather than isolated within a properly rendered/obscured widget) may indicate an accessibility or implementation concern worth a technical review, though this is an observation, not a confirmed defect.
recommendations: Before any rebuild or content migration, confirm with the Imvusa client (in writing) the single correct, current phone number for the George office and correct any page showing the outdated/incorrect value.

Before any rebuild or content migration, confirm with the Imvusa client (in writing) the single correct, current physical address for the Bloemfontein office and correct any page showing the outdated/incorrect value.
Remove the duplicated services card list on the Services page so each service appears once, improving content clarity and avoiding duplicate-content concerns.

Standardize the fabric supplier's brand name spelling to the partner's actual official spelling (confirm with client or supplier which of 'Hertex' or 'Hertext' is correct) and apply consistently sitewide.

Schedule a visual/design review of the Leather Couches and Gallery pages specifically, since they are predominantly image-based and could not be fully evaluated via text extraction; confirm image alt text, load performance, and whether any pricing or model info is embedded in images.
Maintain the current no-pricing approach on the rebuilt site, consistent with the custom-quote business model, unless the client explicitly requests a shift toward published starting-price ranges.
Review the CAPTCHA implementation on the contact-related pages for accessibility and correct rendering behavior as part of the technical/QA stage.
Scope a dedicated competitor-intelligence task explicitly if competitive positioning research is needed for this project, since none was performed or available for this report.

inputArtifacts.title: Imvusa Site Blueprint (Stage 2)
inputArtifacts.summary: This blueprint restructures the existing Imvusa Furniture site (Home, Leather Couches, Gallery, Services, Contact Us) around its true business model: a two-location, lead-generation/consultation business for custom furniture, reupholstery and interior services, not an ecommerce store. It keeps the familiar nav but adds justified pages (a proper Get a Quote flow, an About/Our Story page, and location-specific contact detail without duplicating the authoritative contact block), gives Leather Couches and Gallery real editorial content strategies instead of image-only walls, and resolves the two directly-observed data mismatches (George phone, Bloemfontein address) plus the duplicated services list and Hertex/Hertext spelling inconsistency via a single source-of-truth approach. All journeys funnel toward one core conversion action: submitting a quote/consultation request, backed by one canonical, reused contact block.

sitemap.title: Home
sitemap.purpose: Introduce Imvusa Furniture's custom furniture, reupholstery and interior services across both locations; communicate value proposition and drive visitors toward requesting a quote or consultation. Displays the single canonical contact block (via shared component), not a locally-authored copy of contact details.

sitemap.title: Services
sitemap.purpose: Present the full service list (Furniture Repairs, Reupholstery, Custom Curtains, Headboards, Scatter Cushions, Leather Couches, Wallpaper, Ottomans) exactly once, each with a clear description and a per-service 'Request a Quote' call to action. Replaces the current page's duplicated card list with a single authoritative listing, and standardizes the fabric supplier name as 'Hertex Fabrics' throughout.

sitemap.title: Leather Couches
sitemap.purpose: Serve as the flagship showcase for leather couch craftsmanship: pairs curated photography with real editorial content - material/leather-grade explainers, the customization process, care guidance, and featured client transformations - so the page informs and builds trust rather than functioning as an image-only gallery, and ends with a clear quote-request call to action.

sitemap.purpose: Showcase completed projects across all service lines (not just leather) organized into filterable categories (Reupholstery, Curtains, Headboards, Cushions, Wallpaper, Ottomans) with short project captions describing the brief, fabric/material used (using standardized 'Hertex Fabrics' naming where relevant), and location (George or Bloemfontein), turning the portfolio into evidence that supports conversion rather than an unlabeled image wall.

sitemap.purpose: Introduce the Hertex Fabrics partnership and the four named collections (ADORN, CAPPADOCIA, COASTLINES, ESQUIRE) with representative imagery and short descriptions, consistently spelled 'Hertex' throughout, giving customers a starting point for fabric selection ahead of a quote consultation.

sitemap.title: About Imvusa
sitemap.purpose: Build trust by explaining the business's story, craftsmanship approach, and presence in both George and Bloemfontein; reasonable addition justified by the two-location, relationship-driven consultation model and the absence of any 'about' content in the current nav.

sitemap.title: Get a Quote
sitemap.purpose: Dedicated conversion page with a structured quote-request form (service type, location, project description, photo upload, preferred contact method) that serves as the single primary conversion destination linked from every service, gallery, and location page - replacing generic 'contact us for a quote' scattered messaging with one clear funnel.

sitemap.title: Contact Us
sitemap.purpose: House the single authoritative contact block - one verified phone number, email, and physical address per location (George and Bloemfontein) - reused as a shared component on Home and any other page that displays contact info, eliminating the previously found phone/address mismatches by having exactly one editable source of truth.

Rebuild the Services page from a single structured list of the 8 services (Furniture Repairs, Reupholstery, Custom Curtains, Headboards, Scatter Cushions, Leather Couches, Wallpaper, Ottomans) rendered once via a repeatable card component, eliminating the previously found duplicated back-to-back listing at both the content and template level so it cannot recur on future edits.

Replace the current inline, plain-text-rendered CAPTCHA challenge (found differing between 'select the cup' on Home and 'select the heart' on Contact Us) with a single standardized, properly isolated CAPTCHA/spam-protection widget used consistently on the one quote form and one contact form, flagged separately as an AMBER security/accessibility fix requiring human review before implementation since it touches form security tooling.

content.direction:
DISCLOSURE: This is a genuinely blind run. I have no browsing capability and no image-analysis tool in this environment, and I have not seen and cannot see the actual Imvusa site, its leather couch photography, gallery images, or any real brand assets (logo, existing color usage, fonts). Everything below is a proposed starting hypothesis derived only from the text of the research_report and site_blueprint (positioning: custom furniture / reupholstery / interior services, craftsmanship-led, warm and upscale-but-approachable, two South African regional locations, Hertex Fabrics partnership). Every palette, typography, spacing, component and imagery recommendation in this artifact MUST be verified by a human against real site photography, the actual leather couch and gallery imagery, and any existing brand guidelines before it is treated as approved. Do not implement any of this in code or design tooling without that human visual verification step, per the BUILD -> PREVIEW -> HUMAN DESIGN APPROVAL pipeline.

Design rationale (hypothesis): the brand sits between artisanal craftsmanship and everyday accessibility - it should feel like a well-made leather couch in a warm living room, not a cold corporate showroom. The system leans on warm neutrals and leather/wood-inspired tones, a confident-but-friendly serif or slab display face paired with a clean humanist sans for body copy, generous breathing room to let photography (couches, fabric swatches, finished rooms) carry the emotional weight, and calm, trustworthy CTA color for the single 'Get a Quote' conversion path that the blueprint centers the whole site around.

Card and section surfaces, subtly warmer than base background

palette.usage: Primary brand color - deep saddle-leather brown for headers, nav accents, icons
Secondary leather/tan tone for hover states and secondary accents
Warm brass/ochre accent for highlights, dividers, small decorative details
Primary call-to-action button color (e.g. Get a Quote) - warm terracotta-brick, distinct from brown palette so CTAs stand out without feeling corporate-blue
Primary body and heading text - near-black warm charcoal, not pure black
Secondary text, captions, metadata (e.g. gallery project captions, location tags)
Hairline borders, card outlines, form field borders
Form success/confirmation states (e.g. quote form submitted)
Form validation errors on Get a Quote and Contact forms

typography.usage: Page titles, hero headlines, section headers - conveys craftsmanship and warmth

typography.family: Humanist sans-serif, e.g. 'Inter' or 'Source Sans 3' (PROPOSED - verify)
typography.usage: Body copy, service descriptions, form labels, navigation - optimized for legibility and approachability

typography.family: Same as font.display, slightly smaller weight (PROPOSED)
typography.usage: Pull quotes, fabric collection names (ADORN, CAPPADOCIA, COASTLINES, ESQUIRE), captions needing warmth

components: Primary Nav (Home, Leather Couches, Gallery, Services, Fabrics & Collections, About, Contact) with sticky Get a Quote CTA button
Hero section with full-bleed photography placeholder + headline + single primary CTA
Service Card (icon/image, title, 1-2 sentence description, 'Request a Quote' link) - single canonical instance, no duplication, per blueprint fix
Canonical Contact Block component (phone, email, address per location) reused identically across Home, Contact, and location pages to eliminate data-source mismatches
Gallery Grid with category filter chips (Reupholstery, Curtains, Headboards, Cushions, Wallpaper, Ottomans) and project caption overlay (brief, material, location)
Fabric Collection Card (collection name, representative swatch image placeholder, short description) standardized to 'Hertex Fabrics' spelling
Get a Quote multi-step form (service type, location, project description, photo upload, preferred contact method) with progress indicator
Editorial content block for Leather Couches page (material/leather-grade explainer, process steps, care guidance, featured transformation) alternating text/image layout
Footer with canonical contact block, service links, social links, and legal/privacy line

imageryDirection: DISCLOSURE: no real Imvusa photography has been viewed or analyzed in this run; the following is a proposed art-direction brief for human designers to apply once real site photography (leather couches, gallery projects, fabric swatches) is reviewed.
Favor warm, natural, low-contrast lighting reminiscent of a lived-in but upscale home interior - avoid harsh studio white-backgrounds.
Prioritize close-up, tactile detail shots (leather grain, stitching, fabric texture, wood joinery) alongside wider room-context shots, to reinforce craftsmanship positioning.
Leather Couches page imagery should be paired with real editorial captions (material, leather grade, process step) rather than presented as an unlabeled image wall, per blueprint direction.
Gallery imagery should be consistently captioned with project brief, material/fabric used (standardized 'Hertex Fabrics' naming), and location (George or Bloemfontein).
Fabric collection imagery (ADORN, CAPPADOCIA, COASTLINES, ESQUIRE) should show swatches in situ (draped on furniture) rather than flat swatch-only shots, once real assets are available for review.
Avoid stock-photo furniture imagery wherever possible; flag to human reviewers any pages currently relying on generic stock rather than real Imvusa project photography.
All final imagery choices require human visual verification against actual site/gallery photography before implementation - this agent has not seen that photography.

seoArchitecture: Primary nav and URL structure mirrors the blueprint sitemap: /, /services, /leather-couches, /gallery, /contact - kept flat and shallow for a local lead-gen business, avoiding unnecessary depth.
Home (/) targets brand + broad category intent ('custom furniture George Bloemfontein', 'reupholstery South Africa') and funnels internal links to /services and /contact.

Services (/services) targets service-list intent as a single authoritative hub page listing all 8 services once (Furniture Repairs, Reupholstery, Custom Curtains, Headboards, Scatter Cushions, Leather Couches, Wallpaper, Ottomans) - resolves the duplicate-content issue found in research, which was actively harming this page's crawl/index clarity.

pages.h1: Custom Furniture & Reupholstery, Made to Fit Your Home
sections: Hero: Warm introduction to Imvusa Furniture as a custom furniture, repair, reupholstery and interior services business serving clients from studios in George and Bloemfontein. risks: This is a genuinely blind planning pass: no U-Proof, no prior client knowledge, no browsing or image-analysis tool access, and no execution on any live/staging system. Every ticket below is a proposal for human review, not a verified fact.

The George phone number mismatch cannot be resolved by this pipeline — the plan can only route both candidate values into one editable global template; a human/client must confirm which number is actually correct before either the Contact Block or the Fix-George-Phone ticket can be marked complete.
The Bloemfontein address mismatch has the same limitation: this plan cannot determine which address is correct, only that there must be exactly one going forward, pending human confirmation.

design_system v1 explicitly discloses that every color, font, and imagery recommendation is an unverified hypothesis with no access to real site photography, logo, or brand assets — implementing the Global Design System ticket as final without human visual verification would violate the BUILD -> PREVIEW -> HUMAN DESIGN APPROVAL doctrine.

content_pack v1 does not include copy for the blueprint-added About and Get a Quote pages (it explicitly scoped only Home, Services, Leather Couches, Gallery, Contact Us). Building these pages now risks shipping placeholder/lorem content that must not be mistaken for approved copy.

No real photography has been supplied for Leather Couches or Gallery pages; editorial content tickets will need placeholder image slots, and launching with placeholders risks looking unfinished if not tracked as an explicit pre-launch QA item.

Wiring the Get a Quote form to live email/CRM delivery is out of scope for this AMBER planning pass and must go through separate explicit human approval and QA/regression testing before any real lead data flows through it.

Because this run had no tool access, none of the proposed scope, copy mappings, or component structures have been checked against the actual current live Imvusa site; the 'de-duplication' and 'mismatch fix' tickets are based solely on the research_report/blueprint's description of the problem, not a fresh direct observation.

No ecommerce/WooCommerce component exists in this plan per task instruction; if the client's real business model includes any transactional element not disclosed in the supplied artifacts, this plan would need to be revised.

All permission levels assigned here are AMBER or GREEN per doctrine (no RED, no payments/DNS/registrar actions), but every AMBER ticket still requires explicit human approval before any execution — this plan authorizes nothing on its own.

inputArtifacts.title: Imvusa QA Report (Stage 6)
inputArtifacts.summary: Independent QA review of planning artifacts (research_report, site_blueprint, design_system, content_pack, build_plan) for Imvusa Furniture. The pipeline handles the two core contact mismatches reasonably well on paper: content_pack and build_plan both commit to a single canonical Contact Block and explicitly refuse to guess between the conflicting George phone number / Bloemfontein address, deferring to AMBER human-confirmation tickets rather than silently picking one. The duplicated Services list and Hertex/Hertext spelling issues are also explicitly ticketed and addressed with a single-authoritative-list and standardized-spelling approach. design_system's 'no real visual input' limitation is carried forward honestly and prominently (explicit DISCLOSURE block, all values marked PROPOSED - verify, AMBER gating on the global style ticket). However, several defects remain: (1) content_pack's own summary text still contains the literal historical mismatch values in places, and because content_pack was only provided as a truncated preview, I cannot fully verify that NO page in the pack re-authors contact details outside the canonical block — this is a material verification gap, not a clean pass. (2) The image CAPTCHA discrepancy/security-accessibility risk flagged in research_report is never mentioned again in site_blueprint, design_system, content_pack, or build_plan — it appears to have been silently dropped rather than ticketed or explicitly deferred. (3) content_pack and site_blueprint both add net-new pages (Get a Quote, About, Fabrics & Collections, location subpages) beyond the five pages research_report actually audited; while framed as blueprint-justified extensions and not fabricating new services/locations/awards, build_plan's scope includes these without a visible traceability note tying each new page back to explicit approval rather than agent-invented scope creep. (4) No invented services, locations, certifications, or awards were found — this claim is honestly self-limited and appears consistent with source evidence. (5) Because content_pack and build_plan content bodies were truncated in this handoff, this review cannot certify full-document consistency; readiness is capped accordingly.

The summary text claims a single canonical contact block is used identically everywhere and that no separate contact detail is re-authored, but the full page-by-page content (Services, Leather Couches, Gallery, Contact Us bodies; remaining build tickets) was not available for this audit to confirm the claim holds across every page instance rather than just the Home section described in the preview.

defects.title: New pages (Get a Quote, About, Fabrics & Collections, location subpages) introduced without explicit client-approval trace, risking scope creep beyond audited/approved content
defects.evidence: research_report only audited Home, Leather Couches, Gallery, Services, Contact Us. site_blueprint and build_plan add Get a Quote, About Imvusa, Fabrics & Collections, /contact/george, /contact/bloemfontein as new pages, and content_pack's own summary notes it deliberately excluded Get a Quote/About copy because 'the task scope named' only the original five pages. This is a reasonable editorial judgment but there is no visible record of human sign-off treating this page-count expansion as approved scope versus agent-originated scope creep, which should be explicitly confirmed at HUMAN DESIGN APPROVAL rather than assumed clean by QA.

defects.title: George phone / Bloemfontein address remain genuinely unresolved facts blocking launch
defects.evidence: build_plan explicitly creates AMBER tickets 'Fix George Phone Number Mismatch' and 'Fix Bloemfontein Address Mismatch' that are blocked pending human/client confirmation of the real-world correct values; content_pack's canonical contact block cannot yet contain verified data. This is correctly handled as a hold rather than a silent guess, but it means the site cannot be launched with valid contact info until a human explicitly confirms both facts — this must remain a recorded launch hold, not silently cleared by any later stage.

defects.title: design_system's 'no real visual input' limitation is honestly disclosed but not yet gated by a concrete re-verification ticket in build_plan beyond the general AMBER flag
defects.evidence: design_system v1 contains an explicit DISCLOSURE that no browsing/image-analysis capability was available and every color/typography value is a PROPOSED hypothesis requiring human visual verification against real site photography before implementation. build_plan's Global Elementor Design System Setup ticket is marked AMBER and includes a doNotChange note referencing this, which is good, but there is no distinct, separately trackable 'Human Visual Verification of Palette/Type Against Real Photography' ticket/checkpoint called out as its own line item — it's folded into a general implementation ticket, increasing risk that verification could be treated as done once the ticket is merely 'approved' rather than genuinely visually checked against real assets.

defects.title: Hertex/Hertext and duplicated-services fixes are ticketed but full page-level enforcement not fully visible due to truncation
defects.evidence: content_pack summary states fabric supplier name is standardized to 'Hertex Fabrics' throughout and the duplicated services list is eliminated to a single listing; site_blueprint and build_plan corroborate this intent. However, since content_pack's full page content was truncated in this handoff, per-page confirmation (e.g., that Gallery captions and any footer/CTA mentions also use 'Hertex' rather than 'Hertext') could not be independently verified in this pass.

knowledge.title: Every build passes through the safety pipeline
knowledge.content: BUILD -> PREVIEW -> HUMAN DESIGN APPROVAL -> QA -> FINAL REGRESSION AUDIT -> CONTROLLED ACTIVATION TESTING -> HUMAN LAUNCH APPROVAL -> LIVE. No stage may be skipped by an agent.

knowledge.title: GREEN / AMBER / RED permission tiers
knowledge.content: GREEN actions run automatically. AMBER actions require explicit human approval before execution. RED actions (DNS, registrar, payment credentials, destructive infrastructure) are never executed by an agent without explicit, named authorization.

knowledge.title: Launch never auto-approves
knowledge.content: QA at zero is necessary, never sufficient, for launch. Launch requires human approval; approving with open launch holds is a deliberate, recorded human decision.

knowledge.title: Agents propose; humans approve knowledge
knowledge.content: Agents may propose lesson candidates. No agent may promote its own output into AGENCY or DOCTRINE knowledge. Human approval is the only path from CANDIDATE to APPROVED.
